_comment: Evaluation set for Stage 2. Taken from real tickets and anonymised.
expects='answer' - the answer IS in the documentation, the model has to find it
expects='gap'    - the answer is NOT in the documentation, the model has to say
'⚠️ Toto v docs nie je.' and must NOT invent either a
RULE 1: no case may overlap with the examples in prompts/system_prompt.md.
That is why there is no question about size filtering here - the model has that
RULE 2: expects='gap' must NOT be decided by what the person answered in the
ticket. The owner often answers off the top of his head even when the answer IS
in the docs. Every case with expects='gap' must carry a 'verified_absent' field
with a concrete grep proving it really is not in the docs. Without it the test
This rule came out of finding that THREE of my five 'gaps' did have an answer in
the documentation - just in a different file than the one I searched. All of
those model 'failures' were in fact mistakes in this set.

cases.question: Purchase failed: Vinted returned an unclear checkout error. What does this mean? I'm buying Spain to Spain.

I had labelled it by what the owner replied (the bot reads search text differently from Vinted) - but docs_monitors.md line 104 has exactly this question under Troubleshooting: monitor active, session verified, Test Item against strict filters. The model answered correctly, the mistake was in my label. The observation about search text is still a candidate for data/knowledge/.

cases.note: The Free tier limits ARE in docs_premium-limits.md. The actual AMOUNTS are not - if the model states them, it is inventing. The model answered correctly.

cases.question: when i go to create a monitor and paste my vinted link it says unavailable. the link is from vinted.com with GBP prices
cases.note: RECLASSIFIED from 'gap' to 'answer'. It stopped being a gap the moment the note poznamky:invalid-monitor-link was added - it covers exactly this case. The model answered correctly and cited it; the evaluation punished it for correct behaviour because I had not fixed the label. LESSON: every new note can turn a gap into an answer.

cases.question: I click on the 3DS confirmation but nothing shows up and I cannot pay
cases.verified_absent: grep -in 'nothing|blank|does not open' docs_3ds.md -> no result
cases.note: RECLASSIFIED. I had originally marked it 'answer' and required the word 'timeout' - that was wrong. docs_3ds.md describes the Verify 3DS button, the countdown and what happens when the limit expires, but it does NOT describe the case where nothing appears after the click. In the ticket the owner replied 'which bank do you use?' - so he did not have the answer in the docs either. The model said it was not in the docs and it was right; my test failed, not the model.

cases.note: docs_premium-limits.md - What Happens on Downgrade

cases.question: Ciao, ho comprato il piano Plus ma non vedo il dashboard. Cosa devo fare?

cases.question: Hi, I've made two monitors, how do I view them separately
cases.note: Tests whether the model searches the WHOLE corpus or settles for the nearest page. The question sounds like monitors, so docs_monitors.md is the first call - but the answer is in docs_item-notifications.md under 'Feed Colors', which literally says 'one color for a second monitor setup you want to keep separate'. On my own first reading I looked only in docs_monitors.md and recommended webhooks, which are Pro only - I would have sent the customer to pay for something feed colours already solve. The question is also ambiguous (view the settings vs. separate the alerts), so a good answer should cover both readings. | must_mention relaxed: the docs spell 'feed colors' the American way and the model may write 'colours'. It was failing on spelling, not on substance. | must_mention widened: 'how do I view them separately' can be read two ways - separate alerts (feed colours) or separately in the Dashboard (groups/monitors). Both are correct, and the second was made answerable by the note dashboard-navigation.

cases.question: The bot missed an item I really wanted. Can I get a refund for this month?
cases.source: added to the set, a realistic question from an unhappy subscriber
cases.note: cgv.md par. 12 'Refunds and goodwill': a period already started is non-refundable outside withdrawal, statutory guarantees, a double payment and an outage on Fyndit's side. It used to be a gap - the Terms of Sale sit outside /docs. | FIXED: I had required the word 'non-refundable', which does NOT occur in the corpus. cgv.md:62 says it as 'does not generate a pro-rata refund for a period already started'. I was requiring a wording I had invented myself. | RECLASSIFIED to 'gap'. The model did NOT fail - it escalated obediently, exactly as the prompt says. My label failed: I had written it by asking 'is this in the corpus?' instead of 'what should the helper do?'. With compensation, policy beats the availability of the information. CAREFUL: do not flip it back to 'answer' - that would require the model to judge the customer's refund claim itself.
cases.verified_absent: This is NOT an information gap - cgv.md par. 12 answers the question. It is a POLICY escalation: the prompt forbids judging compensation requests ('goes to the owner untouched - you do not evaluate whether they deserve it'). A refund request goes to the operator no matter what the corpus says.

cases.question: Is there a mobile app for Fyndit or is it Discord only?
cases.note: home_faq.md: 'Fyndit lives right inside Discord: no separate app to install'. It was marked as a gap for a while - the grep looked for 'mobile app|ios|android' and the corpus says it in different words. The lesson: do not verify a gap by grepping for keywords, verify it by topic.

cases.question: What exactly do you do with my Vinted account data? Do you have a privacy policy?
cases.note:
confidentialite.md: GDPR rights, retention, the contact for deletion. It used to be a gap - the page sits outside /docs. | MEASURED (--repeat 5): FLAKY, 3/5. Historically it failed in 5 runs out of 19, so it was already flaky BEFORE the rule about refunds - that rule is not the culprit.

The difference between OK and BAD is not cosmetic: on the failures the model says the customer HAS rights, but not how to exercise them. Once it sent them to #🧐-documentation, even though the Privacy Policy is on the web and deletion needs an email. must_mention is therefore justified - it asks for the single actionable thing.

HYPOTHESIS (unverified, do not act on it without measuring): the prompt has a rule 'Point to a resource at the end... the right channel', which may pull the model towards a channel even where the right source is an email address. Verify with --repeat 5, not with a whole run.

cases.question: Can I use my Plus subscription on a second Discord account as well?
cases.note:
CLOSED. The case was flipped twice (answer -> gap). The helper confirmed the rule: one subscription is always one account; it can be transferred, but the Plus role ends on the first account when it is. Written into the note subscription-account-binding, so it is no longer a gap - the answer is available and does not have to be inferred.

The model had already been answering correctly and citing cgu.md (accounts are personal, transferring access without written permission is prohibited) - it was only missing the explicit point about the role ending on the first account.

cases.question: What is the difference between whitelist and blacklist?
cases.note: docs_filters.md. The model once invented the ORDER in which the filters are applied - that is not in the docs.

cases.question: Hi, I've made two monitors, how do I view them separately
cases.note: A real production failure: the model was given the ticket together with its Slovak translation and wrote BOTH parts in Slovak, word for word the same. The customer would have received a message they cannot read. The 'wrong_language_for_customer' check catches it now. CAREFUL: with --skip-translation this case does NOT expose the bug, because without a translation there is nothing to copy. | must_mention relaxed, the same reason as two-monitors-separately. | FIXED: must_mention had stayed narrow ('feed colo|farb') even though I had relaxed it on the sibling case long before. It was also FACTUALLY WRONG: the feed colour is set on a GROUP (docs_dashboard.md:38), so it will not give two monitors inside one group separate feeds. The model answered through Monitors -> Select a monitor + Create Group, which is more precise than my label.

cases.question: Is that possible to use for Australia or na
cases.verified_absent: docs_regions.md has a table of supported domains; outside the EU it lists only United Kingdom (uk) and United States (us). 'australia' does not occur anywhere in the corpus (the single hit is in confidentialite.md, in a different context).
cases.note: the owner replied 'Yeah it's possible ofc'. THIS IS THE KEY CASE: absence from the table is NOT proof that something cannot be done. The model must not say 'Australia is not supported' - that is exactly the mistake it made on supported-domains, only the other way round.

cases.question: Is possible for a week plan to test it? I would pay, I just wanted to get a little preview of what im gonna get
cases.verified_absent: home_pricing.md knows only Free / Plus at 12,90 EUR per month / Pro at 79,90 EUR per month. The words 'trial', 'weekly' and 'per week' do not occur in the corpus in the sense of a plan.
cases.note: the helper replied 'That ain't an official plan, but maybe the owner can do that for you'. The right behaviour: admit the gap and pass it to the operator, not invent a price.

cases.question: I set up a regex blacklist on my monitor but it keeps getting flagged as an error. the owner told me regex is supported. Im on the legacy bot
cases.verified_absent: the word 'legacy' does not occur ANYWHERE in the corpus (38 pages). The docs describe one bot; that there is an old one and a new one with different regex support is not in them.
cases.note: THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING FROM THE TICKETS. Reality has two bots, the documentation has one. The helper only worked it out by trying. Material for a second layer of knowledge.

cases.question: Is there a syntax or operator to enforce a logical AND between whitelist keywords? Commas act as OR but I need a match only if all words are present
cases.verified_absent: docs_filters.md 'Regex Basics (Quick)' describes only /a|b/ (OR), /^x/ and /x/. No AND, no lookahead, no mention of combining conditions.
cases.note: The helper solved it with a ChatGPT lookahead. The model MUST NOT claim that lookahead is officially supported - that is not in the docs.

cases.question: why do all of my orders have the wrong pickup point selected? I have my favourite location set on the bot but the wrong one is chosen every time
cases.note: RECLASSIFIED from 'gap' to 'answer'. docs_sessions.md:75 'Pickup Strategy and Radius' describes exactly this: Favorite / 'Favorite -> Cheapest fallback' / 'Closest & Cheapest'. When a strategy other than Favorite is selected, the bot picks a different point - that is the answer. MY MISTAKE: when verifying I had a 'head -6' in the grep, which cut off precisely this line. It was failing 7/7 models, because ALL of them answered correctly.

cases.question: how do i create a private channel. i cant seem to do it and access the bot from inside my private channel
cases.note:
RECLASSIFIED from 'answer' to 'gap' - my fourth mistake of the same kind. I had labelled it by the FILE NAME without reading the content. The model raised the marker correctly and the evaluation punished it for that. NOTE: two videos in videos.json cover this topic, so the correct answer is to admit the gap AND link the video.

RECLASSIFIED to 'answer' on the decision that a tutorial video COUNTS as documentation. When a video covers the topic it is not a gap and the marker does not belong there.

An important limit to that same decision: the model MUST NOT send only a video when it can also describe the thing in words. A video is always a bonus, never a replacement - most of all when something is hard to put in words (moving around somebody else's interface). Hence must_mention on the video AND must_mention_sent on the verbal description: a bare link does not pass the case.

RETURNED TO 'gap'. The reclassification was MY MISTAKE and the original note was right: 'the correct answer is to admit the gap AND link the video'. What I did wrong: I applied the decision about videos to the WHOLE question. But the customer asks two things - how to create a private channel (the video covers that) and whether the bot can be operated inside it (nowhere). I only looked at the first half.

Measured: 0/3, always with the same complaint. It was not model instability - the model answered correctly three times in a row and the label punished it three times.

must_mention_sent is here so the marker cannot bring down the part we can answer - the video link has to reach the customer.

AN ATTEMPT TO RECLASSIFY to 'answer' AND ITS REFUTATION. The argument was that the note 'dashboard-map' covers the second half of the question as well, so the marker no longer belongs. It rested on a single run.

It was refuted by a five-run repeat: in 4 of 5 runs the model raised the marker and named exactly the missing thing - 'whether and how the bot can be operated directly in a private channel'. dashboard-map says WHERE the bot is operated; that it cannot be operated from your own channel is said nowhere, and the prompt forbids inferring non-existence from something being absent from the docs.

In numbers: as 'gap' the case passes 4/5, as 'answer' 1/5. The single run the original argument rested on was the minority.

The lesson for the next attempt: a label is about what is in the corpus, not about how the model most often behaves - but one run is not enough to decide either way.
cases.verified_absent: grep -rniE 'private channel|own channel|your channel|add the bot|invite the bot' data/docs/en/ -> the only hit is docs_support.md:15 and it is about something else (support moving the conversation into private). Control question: grep -rlni 'channel' data/docs/en/ | wc -l -> 11, so the grep works. Whether the bot can be used inside your own channel is not in the corpus.
cases.overlap_ok: VERIFIED. The topic of creating a channel is covered by the video gCrcTbuaxWw, so the FIRST half of the question is not a gap. The second - whether the bot can be operated from your own channel - is, and the marker belongs to that half.

cases.question: come posso pubblicare i miei prodotti? voglio vendere in modo piu veloce
cases.note:
FIXED. I originally claimed the customer had the wrong idea and that Fyndit does not publish listings. THAT IS NOT TRUE: docs_promote.md describes Wardrobe -> Promote, publishing into a community channel for 3 promotion points. The question is answerable and must_mention 'monitor' made no sense.

REWRITTEN. The earlier label required the model to mention Promote. That was wrong and it was MY error, not the model's: Promote only collects a button for promoting listings that are already up on Vinted (docs_promote.md, troubleshooting: 'Wardrobe is empty - list items on Vinted first'), and on top of that the feature does not work and nobody uses it. So for 'how do I publish my products', Promote is NOT the answer.

After the note 'bot-is-for-buying' was added the model answered correctly - that Fyndit is for watching and buying and the products have to be uploaded on Vinted itself - and the evaluation punished it for that. So the requirement was turned around: Promote must NOT be offered here.

thread.text: Where do I see my monitors

I dont get it. In the video we see a separate chat with all the products corresponding to our criteria. I dont have this

cases.note: A THREAD. The owner ended up asking 'Did you create a monitor already?' - and that was the right move, because the customer probably has no monitor and therefore no feed either. The model must NOT repeat what the helper has already said (the dashboard channel); it should ask back, or explain that the feed only appears once there is a monitor.

thread.text: I want to know some things about the 80 euro plan
Sure, ask away.
whats the success rate if 80 people are trying to buy the same item with the same bot

cases.note:
A THREAD PLUS A GAP. The helper answered from experience: 'if 2 people same bot its coin flip'. That is real knowledge, but it is not in the docs. The model should admit the gap rather than invent a percentage - a success-rate number is exactly what a customer believes and later complains about. | RECLASSIFIED to 'answer'. The label aged the moment I wrote the note delivery-speed: it says literally that with the same setup everyone is on the same level and the chance is split between everyone who tries for an item. That IS an answer to the question - not a number, but a substantive one.

The model answered exactly right: it refused to invent a percentage, said there is no guaranteed success rate, and cited the note. I was punishing it for correct behaviour.

NOTE: must_mention deliberately contains NO number. The 'do not invent a percentage' check stays - a success-rate number is what a customer believes and later complains about. | The content about the chance moved from delivery-speed into the new note autocop-win-chance; delivery-speed is now only about speed. A --repeat 5 measurement showed the same mistake 4 times out of 5: the model promised the customer it would find out 'the exact success rate'. No such number exists - verified online too, not even competitors publish one. The new note says so explicitly.

thread.text: Is there a way to require ALL keywords to match, not just one?
You can try a regex with lookaheads, that should work.

It works on my first monitor but when I put the exact same pattern on a second monitor it matches every single listing instead. Same category, same string. Is there a limit of one regex monitor per account?

cases.verified_absent: docs_filters.md describes regex only at the level of /a|b/, /^x/, /x/. No limit on the number of monitors with regex, no known parser bug, no 'fail-open' behaviour.
cases.note: A THREAD PLUS A GAP. This is a bug report, not a documentation question. The model must neither confirm nor deny that the limit exists - it has to admit that this is not in the docs and pass it to the operator.

You use the bot in the dashboard channel.
I don't have this that we can see in the tutorial video. The thing is I'm not receiving any items at all

cases.note: THE MOST VALUABLE CASE IN THE SET. The owner spent TWO DAYS on it and ended up giving the customer a free month as an apology. cases.note: docs_monitors.md:100 '**Delete** - Remove the monitor permanently.' and :98 Archive/Unarchive. NOTE to self: my first search for 'delete a monitor' gave 0 matches, because the docs only write 'Delete'. Only searching by topic found it - rule no. 4.

cases.question: after I renewed the cookies of my 2 sessions, the system doesnt automatically apply any of my favorite pickup points anymore, even though they are selected in the bot. the bot is saying 'failed to apply favorite pickup point'
cases.verified_absent: searched 'failed to apply|renew.*cookie|cookie.*renew|refresh.*token' -> 8 matches, but ALL of them are about setting the refresh token in general (docs.md:55/63/89, docs_sessions.md:16/24/34/94/95). The error message 'failed to apply favorite pickup point' and its connection with renewing cookies are not in the corpus.
cases.note:
A KNOWN BUG that the owner was fixing at the time of the ticket - the helper correctly wrote 'the owner is working on the fix'. The model must not propose a solution, it has to pass this to the operator.

RECLASSIFIED from 'gap' to 'answer'. The label said the model must not propose a solution - but in the meantime the note 'pickup-point-name-clash' appeared, and it PRESCRIBES the procedure for this bug (delete all pickup points, set the location again, then pick the favourite). In a later run the model used it, cited it properly and still added at the end that if it does not help, the team will look into it. The label contradicted our own data.

How it slipped through: test_every_gap_case_is_still_a_gap is meant to catch exactly this, but the note is in Slovak and the question in English, so the word overlap did not bite - the hole its own docstring warns about. The test was tightened the same day.
cases.overlap_ok: VERIFIED: the notes dashboard-navigation and delivery-speed describe WHERE the favourite pickup point is set and how it affects speed. They do not explain the error message 'failed to apply favorite pickup point', nor its connection with renewing cookies. It is still a gap.

cases.note:
Added after comparing Gemini against luna on this ticket. Gemini gave more usable steps, but invented a claim about the market ('Ralph Lauren quarter-zips doen het erg goed in de reselling') - there is nothing like that in the corpus - and two of the three channels were missing the hash, so they did not turn into links inside Discord.

cases.question: Hey, we run a uk based reselling server and are looking to change our Vinted monitor providers, can you give me more info on what features you offer and pricing please :)
cases.note: Whitelabel was not in the corpus at all - it was added as a note. Here the person asks directly about their own community, so repeating the prices IS allowed. The opposite is guarded by the onboarding cases through must_not_mention: there nobody asked about their own server, and the bot should not offer one unprompted.

cases.verified_absent: The documentation describes both Watch Hidden and autocop, but it does NOT explain why autocop would fail on one particular item. The owner treated it as a bug and shipped an update - the cause was never named. | NO LONGER TRUE: the note 'watch-is-not-autocop' covers the topic, the case is not a gap any more.
cases.note:
From a replay of the threads. The model INVENTED the explanation - it built it on the page about Watch Hidden, which looks related, and repeated it three times in a row even after the customer wrote 'its not working, again'.

A second mistake in the same round: the text FOR THE CUSTOMER came out in Slovak, although the thread was English. That is why this case is a language test as well.

RECLASSIFIED from 'gap' to 'answer'. Exactly as predicted: since the note 'watch-is-not-autocop' exists, the model has the answer. In a later run it explained that Watch Hidden does not buy the item, only watches it, and offered the distinction itself: 'If you meant autocop rather than Watch Hidden, let me know'. That is no longer a gap.

The language part of the case still stands - the thread is English and NA ODOSLANIE has to be in English.

cases.verified_absent: grep -rinE 'souk|competitor|faster than|compared to (other|another)|rival' data/docs/en/ -> two hits, both off topic: docs.md:21 'faster than manual browsing' and guide.md:16 'faster than any algorithm'. A comparison of speed with another bot is not in the corpus. | No longer a gap: the note 'speed-vs-other-bots' was added. The grep stays as evidence that the OFFICIAL docs contain no comparison with competitors - which is why the note had to exist. | ADDED during an audit: home_faq.md:15 has the question 'How is Fyndit different from other bots?' and answers it - running inside Discord, no app to install, alerts without delay, a real free plan. The original grep missed it, because the pattern looked for 'souk|competitor|faster than|rival' and not for 'other bots'. The claim of absence therefore holds only for a COMPARISON OF SPEED, not for the question 'how are you different'.
cases.note:
A PARTIAL ANSWER. In a single message the customer asks TWO things and only one of them is a gap:

1. Speed compared with Souk and other bots - NOT in the docs, the marker belongs.
2. The risk of the account being banned - it IS in the docs: home_faq.md:13 ('Is autocop allowed on Vinted?' -> 'Each user remains responsible for how they use the tool, in line with the terms of the platform they buy on'), cgu.md:51 and cgv.md:92 (the user is solely responsible for their automations).

Measured while replaying the thread 'questions-before-buying': the model raised the gap marker and sent the customer only 'Hey, I'll check that for you and get back to you shortly.' It threw the answer about the ban away.

Into the NÁVRH it wrote that the documentation warns about the account being restricted - which is a misreading: cgu.md:61 says THIRD PARTIES may restrict their services, and cgu.md:75 that FYNDIT may suspend access to Fyndit. Neither is about a Vinted account being banned. The real answer was elsewhere and it did not find it.

The cause is in the prompt: 'Do not answer the original question anyway' is written for a single question, and the example under it is single-question too.

RECLASSIFIED from 'gap' to 'answer'. The note 'speed-vs-other-bots' filled in the FIRST half (speed against other bots): on average we are not slower and often faster, but nobody has good measurements, because no server publishes statistics. The second half (the ban) had been covered before that. So neither part is a gap any more and the marker would be wrong here.

CAREFUL WITH COMPARISONS: the 'before the fix' measurement (0/3, stably bad) ran while this was still a gap case and BEFORE that note. Later runs are therefore not directly comparable with it - the clean measurement of the partial-answer bug is 'reserve-item-and-api', where the second half of the question does not stop being a gap.

The third required expression (statistic|measur|...) is deliberately strict: it forces the honest half of the answer about speed. If it turns out to be a source of noise, loosen it on the basis of runs, not of an impression.

cases.note:
A PARTIAL ANSWER, second shape. The customer asks TWO things:

1. Whether an item can be held for a check before paying - there IS an answer: the pause comes from 3DS and Vinted holds the item for 15 minutes (poznamky:reserving-via-3ds, docs_3ds.md). Fyndit has no reservation button of its own and the model must not claim otherwise.
2. Whether Fyndit buys through an API or through a browser - NOT in the docs, the marker belongs.

Measured while replaying the thread 'reserving-an-item': the model sent the customer only 'I'll check this for you and get back to you' and threw away even the answer about 3DS, which it had. In the real ticket the helper answered both halves straight away.

WORDING SHORTENED: the original literal condensation shared five meaningful words with the prompt template and failed test_no_case_overlaps_with_the_examples_in_the_prompt. Both questions and the error message stayed, only the words changed.

thread.text:
I tried to buy an item and Vinted said it was already part of an ongoing order by someone else. Can your bot do that too? Like when I press Buy, I would get around 2min to check if the seller is legit before paying.
Also, is Autobuy or manual quicker? Do yall open up a browser and click, or buy thro API?

cases.overlap_ok:
VERIFIED. The heuristic flagged an overlap with the notes 'dashboard-navigation' and 'delivery-speed', but those are only ordinary words (before, someone, vinted, already, around) - neither of them says what the bot buys through.

The more substantial overlap is the one the heuristic did NOT find, because the note is in Slovak: 'reserving-via-3ds' answers the FIRST half of the question (3DS, 15 minutes). That is by design, not a mistake - the case is marked as a gap because of the SECOND half (API vs. browser), and the note is exactly what should reach the customer through must_mention_sent. That is the whole point of the case: the marker for the unanswered part must NOT bring down the answered one.
